cards.explanation: The answer is the whole land. The LORD showed Moses the whole land, from Gilead as far as Dan, all of Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah as far as the Western Sea (Deuteronomy 34:1-2). That's a view you'd want to take a picture of, friends. Moses gets the full tour from one mountaintop, and I can't even find my own spatula without a search party.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross into it." (Deuteronomy 34:4) So the seeing is true, and the crossing is the part that's not happening, friends. Moses gets the view, and he doesn't walk in.

The answer is the LORD Himself. The text says, "And He buried him in a valley in the land of Moab facing Beth-peor…" (Deuteronomy 34:6). The "He" there is the LORD. Moses is called the servant of the LORD (Deuteronomy 34:5), and the LORD Himself buries him. I think that's tender, friends.

The answer is False. The valley facing Beth-peor part is true, but the text says, "…and no one to this day knows the location of his grave." (Deuteronomy 34:6) So nobody knew exactly where he was buried, friends. Even I can lose a whole batch of cookies in my own bakery, but this is a grave, so I'll just say it plainly: the place isn't known.

The answer is good eyes and full strength. The text says, "…yet his eyes were not weak, and his vitality had not diminished." (Deuteronomy 34:7) At a hundred and twenty, friends! I get winded carrying a tray of dough across my own bakery, so I'm taking notes.

The answer is thirty. The Israelites grieved for Moses "…thirty days, until the time of weeping and mourning for Moses came to an end." (Deuteronomy 34:8) That's a whole month of honoring him, bakers. When someone matters that much, you take the time.

The answer is that Moses had laid his hands on him. The text says Joshua "…was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him." (Deuteronomy 34:9) The reason is right there in the verse, bakers. Moses lays on hands, and Joshua steps up filled with wisdom.

The answer is obey. The text says, "So the Israelites obeyed him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Deuteronomy 34:9) Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him. That's a new leader taking over, and the people listened, friends. I would love a crowd that listens like that when I say the oven is hot.

The answer is that the LORD knew him face to face. The text says no prophet has risen in Israel like Moses, "…whom the LORD knew face to face…" (Deuteronomy 34:10) That's the closeness the passage holds up, bakers. Out of everything Moses did, that's the line that sums him up.

The answer is True. The text says no prophet performed "…all the mighty acts of power and awesome deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel." (Deuteronomy 34:12) The whole nation had a front row seat, friends. That's a send-off worth reading twice.
